newsitem.title: USA: Thrifts earned record $1.89 billion in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Thrifts earned record $1.89 billion in second quarter.

text.p: The nation's savings and loans continued to earn profits at a record pace in the second quarter of the year, keeping pace with the strong economy, federal regulators said Thursday.

The Office of Thrift Supervision said savings institutions earned a record $1.89 billion in the quarter, up from $1.35 billion a year earlier. That eclipsed the record of $1.83 billion reported for the first three months of the year.
Net income for the first six months totalled a record $3.72 billion, up from $2.5 billion in the first half of 1995.
The OTS attributed the performance to a strong economy, favourable interest rates, better quality assets, and reduced losses among the 1,397 thrifts that the agency regulates.
"The improvement in profitability has been widespread," Kenneth Ryder, head of research and analysis at the OTS, told a press conference.

Return on average assets was 0.99 percent in the quarter, the highest level since 1959, the OTS said. That was up from 0.96 percent in the first quarter and 0.70 percent in the second quarter of last year.
The OTS said, however, that the total amount of deposits used by thrifts to fund their assets continued to fall.

The agency said the drop in deposits was especially sharp at the 1,370 thrifts that belong to the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF), the fund that protects depositors against losses at failed institutions.
Those thrifts reported deposits falling 6.7 percent on an annualized basis to $454.2 billion at the end of June from $470 billion at the end of 1995.
Deposits now fund just 68.1 percent of thrifts' assets, an all-time-low.
The higher insurance premium that SAIF-insured thrifts pay on deposits contributed to greater use of other borrowings to fund assets, the OTS said.
The OTS counted 33 thrifts on its list of "problem" institutions at the end of the second quarter, down from 37 in the first quarter.
